name: GEF Small Grants Programme Zimbabwe (Low Value Grants)
summary: Zimbabwe's SGP country programme gives low value grants to national NGOs, community groups, Indigenous, women and youth groups for biodiversity, climate and land degradation work, over two years.

eligibility.rule: Represents project beneficiaries or is itself a beneficiary
Not a private-sector, commercial, individual or government applicant
Registered, unless a CBO without a formal organization or association
NGOs and academic bodies have a project manager, finance lead and M&E officer, each with 3 years of experience
Budget excludes overhead such as salaries and office rent, and office running expenses

documents: Completed project budget in the GEF SGP template
Proof of registration, if an NGO or nongovernmental academic institution
Constitution, if an NGO or nongovernmental academic institution
Constitution and registration evidence, if a CBO is not formally organized
Support letters from 3 partners or referees, if previously funded
CVs of 3 key personnel, if an NGO or academic institution
Board member list and certified copies of their IDs
Signed minutes from the last 2 Board meetings
Community consultation minutes, photos and reports as annexes
Project management committee list, if the committee exists

calls.label: Second call for proposals 2026 (Low Value Grants)

status.quote: Proposals must be submitted by the deadline on 22 June 2026 (Zimbabwe time).

deadline.quote: Proposals must be submitted by the deadline on 22 June 2026 (Zimbabwe time).

administered_by.quote: implemented by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) on behalf of the GEF Partnership

applicant_types.quote: national Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), Community Based Organizations (CBOs), Non-governmental academic or educational institutions, Indigenous Peoples organizations, women and youth groups, persons with disabilities, as well as rural communities.

access.quote: The application should be submitted using email address gefsgpzimgrants.zw@undp.org.

window.quote: Proposals must be submitted by the deadline on 22 June 2026 (Zimbabwe time).

amount.quote: Funding limit is USD75,000 though applicant can apply for less amount

effort.quote: Proposals must be submitted by the deadline on 22 June 2026 (Zimbabwe time).
NSC meeting for review of proposals and 9 July 2026 approvals
Revision of proposals by successful 20 July 2026 applicants to address comments raised by NSC.

eligibility.quote: Grant recipients either represent beneficiaries of the project or can be beneficiaries themselves.
Private sector, individuals, commercial entities and government institutions at national, regional and local level, municipalities, etc.) are currently not eligible to receive LVGs.
Proof of registration for the NGOs, non-governmental academic or educational institutions. Exceptions are given to CBOs that have not yet established a formal organization or association

Curriculum Vitae (CVs) of 3 key personnel to manage project in the case NGOs and nongovernmental academic or educational institutions and these include: ▪ Project manager, (with 3 years' experience in Project Management role) ▪ Lead finance person (with 3 years' experience in a finance position) ▪ Monitoring and evaluation person (with 3 years' experience in Monitoring and Evaluation role).

SGP funds do not cover for the following ▪ "Indirect costs" or administrative overhead costs such as staff salaries/fixed monthly allowances and office rent. ▪ Office expenses that include your toiletries, allowances for office cleaner, gardener or items for your office teas.
Only one submission per organization is allowed.

documents.quote: Applicants must, in addition to the proposal, submit a budget in Ms Excel according to GEFSGP budget template
Proof of registration for the NGOs, non-governmental academic or educational institutions.
Applicant must be registered and there is need to provide proof of Registration and Constitution for the NGOs, non-governmental academic or educational institutions.

However, the CBO is requested to submit their Constitution and some form of registration through Statutory bodies like the Environmental Management Agency (EMA), registration though Local Authorities or any government Institution they are working with.
Support letters from at least 3 partners/referees including funding partners if applicant has received previous financial support before this Call for proposals.
Curriculum Vitae (CVs) of 3 key personnel to manage project in the case NGOs and nongovernmental academic or educational institutions and these include:

List of the Board Members and certified copies of their IDs. ix) List of project management committee if it is in existence at the time of proposal development. x) Support letters from local authorities and partners that include funding/donor agencies that have supported the project if the Organisation has previously received funding. xi) Copies of signed minutes for the last 2 Board meetings held
evidence in form of minutes of meetings, photos and reports) for consultations that have been undertaken will be required to be shown in the proposal as Annexes).
